extracted.intended_audience: SBIR Phase II grant applicants and small-biotech teams preparing NIH commercialization and research plans (vaccine developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required components for an NIH PHS 398 SBIR Phase II research and commercialization submission for a vaccine candidate, including specific aims, research strategy, human/animal subject reporting, regulatory milestones, market analysis, IP, finance, and operational plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Research Plan required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Plan must include the listed components: Introduction to Application (Resubmission and Revision), Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Progress Report Publication List, Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety Monitoring Plan, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan, Consortium/Contractual Arrangements, Letters of Support, Resource Sharing Plan(s), Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources, Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each of these sections is an explicit required element in the application (the document lists them in order). Relevant appendices (e.g., study designs, IND budget) should be attached as named appendix items. Failure to provide required sections can render the application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects: Clinical Trial designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Trial? Yes/No. Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial? Yes/No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must indicate whether the proposed project involves human subjects and whether it is an agency-defined Phase III clinical trial. This designation affects required supporting documents (e.g., Data Safety Monitoring Plan, informed consent, human subjects protections) and review/oversight expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals reporting and euthanasia compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are vertebrate animals euthanized? Yes/No. If 'Yes' to euthanasia: Is the method consistent with American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) guidelines? Yes/No. If 'No' to AVMA guidelines, describe method and provide scientific justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full vertebrate animal protocols, describe euthanasia methods and justify deviations from AVMA guidelines. This is required in the Vertebrate Animals section and affects ethical/regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Is program income anticipated during the periods for which the grant support is requested? Yes/No. If 'Yes', use the specified format to reflect the amount and source(s) for each budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If program income is anticipated, detail anticipated amounts and sources by budget period in the application. Leave blank if no program income is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human embryonic stem cells (hESC) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? Yes/No. If Yes, list registration numbers of the specific cell line(s) from the NIH registry or check that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hESC are involved, provide registry identifiers or indicate that a registry line will be used. This is mandatory for compliance with NIH hESC policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents reporting (Renewal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions and Patents: Yes/No. If 'Yes', indicate Previously Reported: Yes/No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal applications must declare inventions/patents arising from the project and whether they have been previously reported; include appropriate disclosures in the inventions section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Investigator / Institution documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: When changing the Project Director/Principal Investigator or Grantee Institution, provide the name and details of the former PD/PI or former institution and complete the change documentation fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete change forms when PD/PI or institution changes to maintain accurate grant records and ensure continuity of funding and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims: clear objectives and measurable milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: The Specific Aims section must state the overall objective and list discrete, testable aims (e.g., Aim 1: Define, optimize, and validate a vaccination regimen; Aim 2: Rodent pharmacokinetics and reproductive toxicology; Aim 3: Request a type C pre-pre-IND meeting with the FDA and prepare a briefing package).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concrete, include tasks/subtasks (e.g., determine route of administration, immune correlates, cross-protective immunity), and be tied to explicit milestones and timelines (Year 1 and Year 2 milestones are enumerated). Milestones provide Go/No-Go decision points and should be achievable within the project period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestones & Timeline for development
rubrics_metrics.description: List of project milestones mapped to calendar/years (e.g., demonstrate route efficacy and cross-protection in Year 1; determine OMV effectiveness and reproductive toxicology and receive agency guidance in Year 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete completion targets by year and link them to subsequent steps (e.g., Phase IIb application, non-human primate studies, IND preparation). Timelines in the commercialization strategy (IND in late 2019, Phase I/IIa complete late 2020, Phase IIb/III in 2021–2022, BLA filing 2H 2023, approval 2H 2024, launch 2025) show expectations and should be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (research significance criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe why the problem is important (e.g., gonorrhea incidence, complications such as PID and infertility, rising antimicrobial resistance, and public health priority as listed by CDC and WHO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a compelling case that the proposed work addresses a major public health need and that expected outcomes would have substantial impact (reduced disease burden, addressing antibiotic resistance). Cite epidemiology and policy priority documents to support significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (research innovation criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain novel aspects (e.g., first reproducible small-animal model inducing protective immunity against N. gonorrhoeae; sustained-release nanoparticulate IL-12 formulation via PIN® technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight technological and conceptual advances over prior failed vaccine attempts and demonstrate why the approach overcomes previously recorded barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (research approach criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe experimental design and methods, including Phase I results that establish proof-of-principle, selection of immunogen (OMV), planned pharmacokinetics and toxicology studies, and methods to determine correlates of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rigorous experimental plans, justification of models and methods, controls, anticipated outcomes, and how data will inform subsequent clinical development and regulatory interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I results and proof-of-principle documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that Phase I milestones were achieved (e.g., induction of gonococcus-specific Th1 cells, generation of anti-gonococcal antibodies, protection against diverse strains, recall responses, and duration of protection for 6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data summaries and figures (e.g., CFU reduction, Kaplan-Meier infection clearance, T cell cytokine responses) to support claims of proof-of-principle; strong Phase I data strengthen Phase II proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory engagement: pre-IND/Type C meeting preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to request a type C pre-pre-IND meeting with the FDA and prepare a briefing package with written questions upon completion of Aims 1 and 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare materials and specific questions for agency feedback to shape toxicology and clinical study designs; document intent and schedule for regulatory interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market analysis and public health need
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate current control measures are inadequate; explain the role of vaccines in preventing resistant bacterial infections and justify why a gonorrhea vaccine would be impactful (CDC priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use epidemiological data, literature on antibiotic resistance, and policy statements (CDC/WHO) to justify market need and public-sector demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market size, pricing, and revenue assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate vaccine market value and pricing benchmarks (e.g., private-sector HPV three-dose cost ~$540; CDC purchase discounts; conservative and aggressive price estimates for a gonorrhea vaccine at $250–$450; assumed public-sector discount ~33%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sensitivity analyses for price points, estimate percent of market likely bought by CDC (>50% plausible), and convert vaccination rates and patient-population assumptions into revenue projections (years 1,5,10). Explicitly state whether international sales are included or excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market penetration & value assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit numbered assumptions to estimate market penetration and value (the document lists 10 assumptions: price determination approach; female-targeted treatment share; public agencies purchasing at volume discount after year 1; infection rate declines due to immunization; population differences; population growth; vaccination rate; increase in vaccination due to visibility; cost and sales to private sector; cost and acceptance into public sector programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and justify each assumption; use conservative and aggressive scenarios; tie assumptions to sources of uncertainty and how they affect revenue projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property protection and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe patents and proprietary rights (e.g., exclusive worldwide licenses from Brown University for PIN® and micronization processes, list of issued and pending patent numbers and countries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide patent lists, license agreements, and explanation of uniqueness (e.g., PIN® does not require emulsification). Clarify territorial coverage, claim scope, and pending applications; discuss how IP underpins commercialization strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization strategy and target market
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline strategy for development and market entry (e.g., file IND, complete clinical phases, target STD clinics and CDC bulk purchasing, partner with major pharma for advanced development and global sales, outsource manufacturing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify go-to-market channels (STD clinics, public programs), potential partners and roles (manufacturing, marketing), outsourcing plans, and strategies to reduce capital requirements. Justify targeting decisions with demographic and clinic distribution data.

rubrics_metrics.name: SWOT analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats pertinent to the company and product (Table 4 referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide candid internal and external analysis to inform risk mitigation and strategic planning; use SWOT to justify partnership/funding needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance plan and fundraising strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed plan to raise specified funds (e.g., raise $2.625M through Series A Preferred Shares in 2017 in addition to SBIR award; limit sale to 16 individual investors at $100,000 each with remaining to seed VC), targeted investor groups, and planned use of proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State fundraising targets, investor types, investor selection strategy, intended use of funds (initiate Phase I/II studies, out-licensing, corporate purposes), and steps to limit shareholder dilution/number of investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production, manufacturing and partner agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to outsource manufacturing, distribution and sales; cite past/managing partners (e.g., Bend Research/Capsugel, Neumedicines) and discuss scale-up and batch consistency achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail manufacturing outsourcing partners, quality management, supply security, and any prior manufacturing relationships. Explain how outsourced production reduces capital needs and ensures GMP/commercial supply capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue streams, royalties, and financial projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Projected revenues by source and year (licensing fees & royalties, grants, investments, product revenue), assumptions such as ~5% royalty post-2022, vaccination rates, and price-per-vaccine scenarios; include operating expenses and EBIT projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multi-year financial tables (revenues, operating expenses, EBIT), show scenario analyses across price points and penetration rates, and explain key drivers of profitability and commercialization timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company commercialization compliance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of compliance with SBIR Phase II award limits: 'Therapyx, Inc. has not received more than 15 SBIR Phase II awards from the Federal Government during the preceding five fiscal years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certify compliance with SBIR program limits on prior Phase II awards; if close to threshold, explain and provide supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appendices with supporting materials such as study designs and quotes, IND budget proposals, letters of support, and other referenced support documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label each appendix item (e.g., 'Appendix 1: Repo study designs and quotes', 'Appendix 2: IND Budget Proposal Master-TherapyX') and ensure critical supporting documents referenced in the Research Strategy and Commercialization Plan are attached.
